claim: Degrons are minimal protein features that are sufficient to target proteins for degradation.
source: Degrons are minimal protein features that are sufficient to target proteins for degradation.
evidence: This is a definitional statement presented in the abstract that establishes the concept of degrons.

claim: In most cases, degrons allow recognition by components of the cytosolic ubiquitin proteasome system.
source: In most cases, degrons allow recognition by components of the cytosolic ubiquitin proteasome system.
evidence: This statement is presented as established knowledge about degron function.

claim: Currently, all of the identified degrons only function within the cytosol.
source: Currently, all of the identified degrons only function within the cytosol.
evidence: This statement summarizes the state of knowledge prior to this study.

claim: The authors identified the first short linear sequences that function as degrons from the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) lumen.
source: Using Saccharomyces cerevisiae, we identified the first short linear sequences that function as degrons from the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) lumen.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: The identified degrons facilitate proteasomal degradation through the endoplasmic reticulum associated degradation (ERAD) system when transferred to proteins.
source: We show that when these degrons are transferred to proteins, they facilitate proteasomal degradation through the endoplasmic reticulum associated degradation (ERAD) system.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: These degrons enable degradation of both luminal and integral membrane ER proteins.
source: These degrons enable degradation of both luminal and integral membrane ER proteins, expanding the types of proteins that can be targeted for degradation in budding yeast and mammalian tissue culture.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing degradation of different protein types in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: The ubiquitin proteasome system accounts for over 80% of protein degradation.
source: The ubiquitin proteasome system is the primary cellular degradation route, accounting for over 80% of protein degradation (Collins and Goldberg, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Collins and Goldberg, 2017.

claim: In Saccharomyces cerevisiae there is 1 E1, 11 E2s, and >60 E3s for ubiquitin.
source: For ubiquitin, in Saccharomyces cerevisiae there is 1 E1, 11 E2s, and >60 E3s whereas mammals have 2 E1s, ~40 E2s, and >600 E3s (Clague et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Clague et al., 2015.

claim: Mammals have 2 E1s, ~40 E2s, and >600 E3s for ubiquitin.
source: For ubiquitin, in Saccharomyces cerevisiae there is 1 E1, 11 E2s, and >60 E3s whereas mammals have 2 E1s, ~40 E2s, and >600 E3s (Clague et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Clague et al., 2015.

claim: The specificity of the ubiquitination process is primarily driven by the E3 ubiquitin ligases.
source: The specificity of the ubiquitination process is primarily driven by the E3 ubiquitin ligases and a major challenge in ubiquitin biology is the identification of the sequences that target proteins for degradation (called 'degrons').
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge in the field.

claim: Degrons are usually short linear motifs and, by definition, are sufficient to confer degradation when transferred to otherwise stable proteins.
source: Degrons are usually short linear motifs and, by definition, are sufficient to confer degradation when transferred to otherwise stable proteins.
evidence: This is a definitional statement about degrons based on established knowledge.

claim: The first degrons to be discovered were at the amino-terminus of proteins.
source: The first degrons to be discovered were at the amino-terminus of proteins (Bachmair et al., 1986) and these N-degrons were eventually summarized as the 'N-end rule' (Varshavsky, 2011), and later the 'N-degron pathways' (Varshavsky, 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Bachmair et al., 1986, Varshavsky, 2011, and Varshavsky, 2019.

claim: All known degrons target cytosolic proteins for ubiquitination and degradation by the proteasome.
source: Even with a wide range of physiological roles for protein degradation, degrons are still unidentified for most E3 ubiquitin ligases. All known degrons target cytosolic proteins for ubiquitination and degradation by the proteasome and the identification of degrons for a few key ubiquitin ligases has enabled exploitation of the proteasome to facilitate targeted protein degradation of 'undruggable' cytosolic proteins (Samarasinghe and Crews, 2021).
evidence: This statement summarizes the state of knowledge prior to this study, supported by citation to Samarasinghe and Crews, 2021.

claim: Over 40% of proteins are translocated into the ER before trafficking to other organelles or secretion from the cell.
source: The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) represents the organelle with the largest flux of proteins, with over 40% of proteins translocated into the ER before trafficking to other organelles or secretion from the cell.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about ER protein trafficking.

claim: ERAD systems are highly conserved among all eukaryotes.
source: At the ER, the primary protein quality control pathways are, collectively, referred to as endoplasmic reticulum associated degradation (ERAD) and these systems are highly conserved among all eukaryotes (Huyer et al., 2004; Vashist and Ng, 2004; Carvalho et al., 2006; Denic et al., 2006; Foresti et al., 2014; Khmelinskii et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: In S. cerevisiae, the Hrd1 complex comprises five proteins: Hrd1, Hrd3, Usa1, Der1, and Yos9.
source: In S. cerevisiae, the Hrd1 complex comprises five proteins: Hrd1, Hrd3, Usa1, Der1, and Yos9.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about the composition of the Hrd1 complex.

claim: Soluble, luminal ERAD substrates are retrotranslocated by hetero-oligomers of Hrd1/Der1.
source: Soluble, luminal ERAD substrates are retrotranslocated by hetero-oligomers of Hrd1/Der1 (Mehnert et al., 2014; Wu et al., 2020; Pisa and Rapoport, 2022), or in some cases, homo-oligomers of Hrd1 (Carvalho et al., 2010; Baldridge and Rapoport, 2016; Schoebel et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Soluble, luminal ERAD substrates are retrotranslocated by homo-oligomers of Hrd1 in some cases.
source: Soluble, luminal ERAD substrates are retrotranslocated by hetero-oligomers of Hrd1/Der1 (Mehnert et al., 2014; Wu et al., 2020; Pisa and Rapoport, 2022), or in some cases, homo-oligomers of Hrd1 (Carvalho et al., 2010; Baldridge and Rapoport, 2016; Schoebel et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Hrd1 is sufficient for the basic functions of ERAD but without the other complex components, loses the specificity that normally defines the system.
source: Hrd1 is sufficient for the basic functions of ERAD but without the other complex components, loses the specificity that normally defines the system (Denic et al., 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Denic et al., 2006.

claim: The ER-tFT was quite stable, while the KHN-tFT was degraded with a half-life of less than 30 min.
source: Using a cycloheximide chase followed by immunoblotting, we found the ER-tFT was quite stable, while the KHN-tFT was degraded with a half-life of less than 30 min (Figure 1B), consistent with previous reports (Vashist et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and is consistent with previous reports.

claim: The two proteins (ER-tFT and KHN-tFT) were distinguishable following cycloheximide treatment using flow cytometry.
source: Using flow cytometry, the two proteins were also distinguishable following cycloheximide treatment (Figure 1C and D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C, D, and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Isoleucine at the first position was present in 17.7% of unstable pentapeptides while leucine was present in 14.8%.
source: The sequencing results of the unstable sorted bin illuminated an enrichment of pentapeptides beginning with isoleucine and leucine (Source data 1). Specifically, isoleucine at the first position was present in 17.7% of unstable pentapeptides while leucine was present in 14.8%.
evidence: This is supported by sequencing data from the pentapeptide library screen.

claim: Isoleucine showed a 3.8-fold enrichment in the unstable dataset based on codon usage.
source: Based on codon usage in a random sampling, isoleucine was predicted to appear 4.7% of the time (3/64 codons) giving a 3.8-fold enrichment in our dataset.
evidence: This is calculated from the sequencing data and codon usage predictions.

claim: Leucine showed a 1.6-fold enrichment in the unstable dataset based on codon usage.
source: Leucine was predicted to appear at a specific position 9.4% of the time (6/64 codons) giving a 1.6-fold enrichment in our dataset (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is calculated from the sequencing data and codon usage predictions, shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Repeats of IHPYW dramatically decreased protein stability, with a 20 amino acid 4X(IHPYW) repeat successfully resembling the KHN control.
source: We found that repeats of IHPYW, one of the most unstable sequences, dramatically decreased protein stability, with a 20 amino acid 4X(IHPYW) repeat successfully resembling the KHN control (Figure 1I and J).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1I and J.

claim: Simply repeating a stable control sequence (GNRWG) did not destabilize the protein.
source: On the other hand, simply repeating a stable control sequence (GNRWG) did not destabilize the protein (control variant 1 [ConV1], Figure 1J).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1J.

claim: The 4X(IHPYW) sequence, called DegV1 (Degron Variant 1), functions as an ER-localized degron.
source: Based on these results, we concluded that the 4X(IHPYW) sequence, which we called DegV1 (Degron Variant 1), functions as an ER-localized degron.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the experimental data showing destabilization of proteins containing this sequence.

claim: Approximately 90% of the ER-targeted construct had the signal sequence removed.
source: Based on the size of the ER-DegV1-NbGFP compared to DegV1-NbGFP, we concluded that ~90% of the ER-targeted construct had the signal sequence removed and uncleaved signal sequence was unlikely to factor into the function of DegV1 (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is inferred from the molecular weight comparison shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Embedding DegV1 after the N-terminal signal sequence destabilized ER-NbGFP with a half-life of approximately 30 min.
source: Using a cycloheximide chase, the ER-NbGFP protein alone was quite stable, but embedding DegV1 after the N-terminal signal sequence destabilized ER-NbGFP with a half-life of approximately 30 min (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The presence of an internal DegV1 made no difference in protein stability when compared to the nanobody alone.
source: To test whether the DegV1 sequence worked within internal loops, we used the same nanobody scaffold but replaced the complementary determining region 3 with DegV1 and found that the presence of an internal DegV1 made no difference in protein stability when compared to the nanobody alone (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Integrating the DegV1 sequence immediately before the HDEL retention signal resulted in no change in the stability of the NbGFP target protein.
source: Testing DegV1 at the C-terminus of the NbGFP was complicated by the requirement for an ER retention signal. We integrated the DegV1 sequence immediately before the HDEL retention signal, and, again, this resulted in no change in the stability of the NbGFP target protein (Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The DegV1 degron was capable of acting as an ER luminal degron, but only when positioned at the N-terminus of ER-localized proteins.
source: Together, these results suggest that the DegV1 degron was capable of acting as an ER luminal degron, but only when positioned at the N-terminus of ER-localized proteins.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the experimental data showing position-dependent effects.

claim: DegV1-targeted luminal ER substrates were degraded by the proteasome.
source: Appending DegV1 immediately after the signal sequence resulted in degradation of ER-GFP (solid blue line), which was inhibited by adding bortezomib (dashed line, panel 2, Figure 2E). This indicated DegV1 targets the luminal ER-GFP for proteasomal degradation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing bortezomib-sensitive degradation in Figure 2E.

claim: DegV1-containing ER-GFP was more stable in an hrd1Δ strain.
source: In contrast, DegV1-containing ER-GFP was more stable in an hrd1Δ strain, and bortezomib resulted in little further stabilization of DegV1-containing GFP (panel 2, Figure 2F, see also Figure 2—figure supplement 1D), possibly from a small fraction being incompletely translocated into the ER.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: When DegV1 was appended to the ER-NbGFP, the protein was unstable, with a half-life of approximately 30 min in a cycloheximide chase.
source: As expected, when DegV1 was appended to the ER-NbGFP, we found the protein was unstable, with a half-life of approximately 30 min in a cycloheximide chase (Figure 2G and H, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2G, H, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1G.

claim: With the notable exception of Yos9, the previously identified components of the ERAD-L complex (Hrd1, Hrd3, Der1, and Usa1) were required for DegV1 degradation.
source: We found that, with the notable exception of Yos9, the previously identified components of the ERAD-L complex (Hrd1, Hrd3, Der1, and Usa1) were required for DegV1 degradation (Figure 2I and J).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2I and J.

claim: The Doa10 ubiquitin ligase was not required for DegV1 degradation.
source: Conversely, the Doa10 ubiquitin ligase was not required (Figure 2I and J).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2I and J.

claim: When DegV1-containing proteins were localized to the cytosol, Hrd1 was not required for their degradation through the proteasome.
source: However, in contrast to ER-localized DegV1, when DegV1-containing proteins were localized to the cytosol, Hrd1 was not required for their degradation through the proteasome (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: DegV1 was able to destabilize the endogenous protein Suc2.
source: With ConV1, Suc2 was stable over several hours, and, based on the modified glycosylation pattern, even appeared to be partially trafficked from the ER. In contrast, with DegV1 Suc2 was dramatically destabilized (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: DegV1 was able to destabilize the integral membrane protein Big1.
source: We replaced the signal sequence of Big1 with the signal sequence of mating factor alpha followed by either DegV1 or ConV1, an HA tag, and the Big1 coding sequence. DegV1 was also able to destabilize the integral membrane protein Big1 (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: DegV1 was capable of driving degradation for the multi-spanning membrane protein Elo1.
source: We found that DegV1 was capable of driving degradation for the multi-spanning membrane protein Elo1 (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: DegV1 functions as an N-terminal degron for endogenous proteins with a range of topologies.
source: These results support that DegV1 functions as an N-terminal degron for endogenous proteins with a range of topologies.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the experimental data showing degradation of different protein types.

claim: Both membrane proteins (Big1 and Elo1) were significantly stabilized upon treatment with bortezomib.
source: Both membrane proteins were significantly stabilized upon treatment with bortezomib (Figure 3D and E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D and E.

claim: DegV1 targets both luminal and integral membrane ER proteins for recognition by ERAD and subsequent degradation by the proteasome.
source: Therefore, DegV1 targets both luminal and integral membrane ER proteins for recognition by ERAD and subsequent degradation by the proteasome.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the experimental data showing proteasome-dependent degradation of different protein types.

claim: The addition of DegV1, but not ConV1, reduced the steady-state ER-mNG levels compared to the control in U2OS cells.
source: We transfected U2OS cells with the ER-mNG containing either ConV1 or DegV1. The addition of DegV1, but not ConV1, reduced the steady-state ER-mNG levels compared to the control (Figure 4A, compare lanes 1, 4, and 7).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: ER-mNG and ER-ConV1-mNG were quite stable after translation inhibition with emetine.
source: When we inhibited translation with emetine, we found that ER-mNG and ER-ConV1-mNG were quite stable (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A and B.

claim: ER-DegV1-mNG was unstable, with a half-life of approximately 4 hr in mammalian cells.
source: In contrast, ER-DegV1-mNG was unstable, with a half-life of approximately 4 hr (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A and B.

claim: Treatment with bortezomib resulted in a dramatic accumulation of ER-DegV1-mNG protein within 8 hr of treatment in U-2 OS cells.
source: In contrast, for ER-DegV1-mNG proteasomal inhibition resulted in a dramatic accumulation of protein within 8 hr of treatment (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C and D.

claim: At 24 hr of bortezomib treatment ER-DegV1-mNG accumulated to similar levels compared to ER-ConV1-mNG.
source: Remarkably, at 24 hr of bortezomib treatment ER-DegV1-mNG accumulated to similar levels compared to ER-ConV1-mNG, suggesting that the low steady-state level of ER-DegV1-mNG was caused by continuous degradation, rather than a general expression problem.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and provides inference about the mechanism.

claim: Treatment with CB5083 resulted in stabilization of ER-DegV1-mNG.
source: Similar to the bortezomib treatment, we found that treatment with CB5083 resulted in stabilization of ER-DegV1-mNG (Figure 4E and F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E and F.

claim: The degradation of ER-DegV1-mNG was completely inhibited when cells were pretreated with either bortezomib or CB5083.
source: When we pretreated cells with either bortezomib or CB5083 and inhibited translation with emetine, we found that the degradation of ER-DegV1-mNG was completely inhibited.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing stabilization with inhibitor pretreatment.

claim: The degron-containing protein (ER-DegV1-mNG) was stabilized in the absence of Hrd1 in mammalian cells.
source: Using either wild-type or Hrd1 knockout cells (Shi et al., 2017), we followed degradation of ER-DegV1-mNG and found that the degron-containing protein was stabilized in the absence of Hrd1 (Figure 4H and I).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4H and I.

claim: DegV1 functions as an Hrd1-dependent ER-localized degron in mammalian cells.
source: Taken together, these data indicate that DegV1 functions as an Hrd1-dependent ER-localized degron in mammalian cells.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the experimental data showing Hrd1-dependent degradation in mammalian cells.

claim: DegV1 works with folded, luminal, and completely soluble proteins as well as integral membrane proteins with differing topologies.
source: We focused on functionalizing these motifs and found that DegV1 works with folded, luminal, and completely soluble proteins as well as integral membrane proteins with differing topologies.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings from the study.

claim: DegV1 works with both exogenous and endogenous proteins that are otherwise stable.
source: It works with both exogenous and endogenous proteins that are otherwise stable.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings from the study.

claim: DegV1 is degraded through the Hrd1-ERAD axis using the proteasome.
source: Importantly, DegV1 is degraded through the Hrd1-ERAD axis using the proteasome (Figures 2 and 3).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: DegV1 works across eukaryotes in the mammalian cell culture system.
source: Furthermore, we found that DegV1 works across eukaryotes in the mammalian cell culture system (Figure 4).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The sequence 'IHPYW' forming the basis of DegV1 appears to be relatively uncommon in nature and is not present in other proteins encoded in the S. cerevisiae genome.
source: However, the sequence 'IHPYW' forming the basis of DegV1 appears to be relatively uncommon in nature and is not present in other proteins encoded in the S. cerevisiae genome.
evidence: This is inferred from analysis of the S. cerevisiae genome.

claim: DegV1 appears to be absent from the currently annotated and available fungal genomes in the Saccharomyces Genome Database.
source: In fact, DegV1 appears to be absent from the currently annotated and available fungal genomes in the Saccharomyces Genome Database (Cherry et al., 2012).
evidence: This is inferred from database analysis, with citation to Cherry et al., 2012.

claim: The degradation rates of degron-containing proteins are similar to the rates of other well-characterized ERAD substrates.
source: It should be noted that the degradation rates of our degron-containing proteins are similar to the rates of other well-characterized ERAD substrates.
evidence: This is inferred from comparison with known ERAD substrates.

claim: DegV1 is degraded in a manner consistent with that of endogenous ERAD substrates.
source: We interpret these results to mean that DegV1 is degraded in a manner consistent with that of endogenous ERAD substrates.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: The retrotranslocation process itself appears to function by unfolding, or mostly unfolding, its substrates.
source: The retrotranslocation process itself appears to function by unfolding, or mostly unfolding, its substrates.
evidence: This is presented as a general understanding of the retrotranslocation process.

claim: Glycosylated ERAD substrate proteins are retrotranslocated across the ER membrane, with the N-linked glycans representing a similar steric challenge compared to secondary structure or smaller folded proteins.
source: What is certain is that glycosylated ERAD substrate proteins are retrotranslocated across the ER membrane, with the N-linked glycans representing a similar steric challenge compared to secondary structure or smaller folded proteins (Grotzke et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Grotzke et al., 2013.

claim: Because DegV1 allows degradation of fully folded proteins, it is possible that the proteins are transported in a fully folded state.
source: Because DegV1 allows degradation of fully folded proteins, it is possible that the proteins are transported in a fully folded state.
evidence: This is speculation based on the experimental observations.

claim: The targeted proteins are likely recognized and transported in an unfolded state after ERAD complex engagement.
source: However, we favor the idea that the targeted proteins are likely recognized and transported in an unfolded state after ERAD complex engagement.
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism based on the authors' interpretation.

claim: The authors have created the first tool that can be used to target proteins for degradation from a previously unreachable cellular localization.
source: Here, we have created the first tool that can be used to begin to answer these outstanding questions. We've identified a genetically encoded sequence that is easily manipulatable for targeting proteins for degradation from a previously unreachable cellular localization.
evidence: This is a summary claim about the significance of the work.

claim: The theoretical amino acid diversity of a pentapeptide library is 3.2 million (20^5).
source: The theoretical amino acid diversity of a pentapeptide library is 3.2 million (205).
evidence: This is a mathematical calculation based on the number of amino acids and positions.

claim: The authors obtained 1.2 million transformants from the pentapeptide library.
source: We transformed the library into wild-type yeast and obtained 1.2 million transformants.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the library generation.

claim: The 'unstable' bin encompassed 4% of the sorted cells.
source: We collected an 'unstable' bin (exhibiting a low mCherry/GFP ratio), which encompassed 4% of the sorted cells, for sequencing (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the FACS sorting, shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: In total, 13 million mCherry-GFP positive events were sorted from the pentapeptide-ER-tFT library.
source: In total, 13 million mCherry-GFP positive events were sorted from the pentapeptide-ER-tFT library, >10 times over the library size.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the FACS sorting.

claim: The sorted cells represented >10 times over the library size.
source: In total, 13 million mCherry-GFP positive events were sorted from the pentapeptide-ER-tFT library, >10 times over the library size.
evidence: This is calculated from the number of sorted events and the library size.
